title: Measure a shape you drew yourself, not just a screenshot
goal: Pick the ruler, switch it to Size, and point at a rectangle you drew a moment ago: nothing lights up and clicking measures nothing. The hint still says click an element for its width and height. The same mode works perfectly over a screenshot you pasted in, so the one thing Size mode cannot measure is the thing you made.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-08 in the probe build. Walk: blank 900x600, key r, drag (300,240)->(560,420), key v, escape, measureMode size, waitFor edgeMap, move to (430,330), wait, click (430,330). Log at /tmp/photonz-playtest/repro-size/log.json: every step after the click reports measures=[] and cue=none. The screen capture size-sc.png shows the pointer dot dead centre on the red rectangle with no highlight and the hint pill still reading "Size  Click an element for its width and height". Contrast: Scripts/playtest/distance-lands-on-release.json step 13 drags in Size mode over settings-pane-2x.png and lands two measurements (Width = 624 px, Height = 44 px), so the element ladder works on picture pixels but not on drawn layers. Distance mode DOES snap to drawn shapes (Scripts/playtest/caliper-catches-a-drawn-edge-walk.json reads 64 px off a drawn box), so the edge map sees them; the gap is in the Size mode element preview. Start at CanvasMeasure.refreshMeasureHoverReadout / drawElementPreview and ElementBounds.
acceptance: Hovering the middle of a shape you drew on a blank canvas highlights that shape and shows its width and height
Clicking it leaves a size measurement on the picture and a row in the Measurements list
Measuring elements in an opened screenshot still works exactly as it does today
One walk under Scripts/playtest proves both, and its log names the measurement it made on the drawn shape

log.note: Reproduced first: Scripts/playtest/size-measures-a-drawn-shape-walk.json on the pre-fix build, blank 900x600 with a 260x180 rectangle, Size mode, hover and click at (430,330) -> measures=[] and the hint unchanged. Cause: snappingEdgeMap and measureLumaField both key off document.layers.compactMap(\.imageRef).first, so Size mode only ever read the backdrop picture. Drawn layers are not in the edge map at all; Distance mode reaches them through MeasureSnapping.layerLines instead, which is why it snapped and Size did not.

Adversarial review before building: the shortest fix is not a better pixel reader but the document itself. The app knows every box it drew, exactly. Two things must NOT become elements: a caliper bounding box (nobody aims at one) and a layer covering the whole canvas (that is the backdrop Size mode reads pixels from, and offering it would turn every miss into a hit on everything).

Adversarial review of the first cut caught a regression for the primary use: drawn rungs were put ahead of every picture rung, so a highlight box drawn around a button hid the button and [ could not reach it. Reworked into ONE ladder nested by size, so the button comes first and ] climbs onto the drawn box. Proven as claims 4 and 5 in the walk.

Shipped: Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerElements.swift (candidates / merged / neighbors, 18 tests written first) wired into CanvasMeasure.refreshMeasureHoverReadout and CanvasMeasure.neighbors. Rotated and slanted layers are skipped on purpose: contentBounds is stored unturned. Walk green at 66 steps: drawn 260x180 and 180 measured exactly, screenshot button unchanged at 124x30 with identical feet, ] climbs to 144x50. Scripts/test.sh green (4862 tests). Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-08-size-measures-a-drawn-shape.json with two real screen captures.
